---
title: "Escalations to PSO"
description: "Calls the call centre escalated to Partner Success and Operations."
---

The number of calls the call centre escalated to Partner Success and Operations
(PSO). The call centre calls these callbacks: the call passes to a higher level
of support, which calls the person back.

## Calculation

Count the distinct calls (`call_no`) in `call_centre.weekly_topic_dump` with a
`transactiontype` of "Callback", over a span of call dates. Every topic row of
an escalated call carries the flag. The examples group by calendar month, but
any span of call dates works.

Start no earlier than 2026-06-29, when escalation to PSO began. Callbacks before
then were not handled the same way.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
SELECT
    date_trunc('month', call_date) AS month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT call_no) AS escalations
FROM call_centre.weekly_topic_dump
-- transactiontype is padded with trailing spaces
WHERE trim(transactiontype) = 'Callback'
  -- set the reporting window; escalation to PSO began on 2026-06-29
  AND call_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-07-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', call_date)
ORDER BY month;
```

## R

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("call_centre", "weekly_topic_dump")) |>
  filter(
    # transactiontype is padded with trailing spaces
    str_trim(transactiontype) == "Callback",
    # set the reporting window; escalation to PSO began on 2026-06-29
    call_date >= as.Date("2026-07-01"),
    call_date <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  group_by(month = floor_date(call_date, "month")) |>
  summarise(escalations = n_distinct(call_no)) |>
  arrange(month)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

**Escalations are rare.** One or two calls can double a month's count, so
compare over long spans and read the count next to the
[escalation rate](escalation-rate.qmd).

**PSOM tickets are a cross-check, not the source.** Each escalation becomes a
ticket on the PSOM Jira board ([`jira.psom`](../../catalog/jira/psom.qmd)),
created the next working day. Match them with
`form_topic LIKE '%Escalated from Call Center%' OR lower(summary) LIKE '%canadalogin callback%'`,
reading each ticket from its own latest snapshot. The summary match catches
PSOM-140 and PSOM-147, two callback tickets with a blank form topic. The two
sources agree call for call, but a ticket count can still differ from this one:
a count on form topic alone misses the blank-topic tickets, and a count by
ticket creation date includes escalations whose calls are not yet in the call
centre data.

The `callback` column in
[`weekly_activity_report`](../../catalog/call_centre/weekly_activity_report.qmd)
holds the same count by Sunday-to-Saturday week. It has no call dates, so it
cannot give calendar months.

## Alternative names

- callbacks
- call centre escalations
- escalated calls
- escalations to Partner Success and Operations
